checklist.notes: Sequencing, the make a decision collocation, and information focus are represented across ordered narrative, form choice, listening, and writing.
Explicit sequencers and controlled collocation practice prepare learners for the four-event account.
Recognition and construction precede listening and an integrated four-sentence writing task.
Instructions and writing constraints clearly state required sequencers and collocation.
The final task combines two known targets but caps output at four one-event sentences.
Familiar names and everyday rainy-day and lost-key contexts are accessible, while collocation selection usefully discourages literal verb transfer.
The set is compact; one four-sentence response is supported by four short preparatory items.

methods: Reviewed the exercise set and audit against the declared original project-authored policy and external-payload/media declarations.

findings.description: Both listening questions elicit the same fact, the bedroom, so the second response adds workload without broadening comprehension evidence.
findings.recommendation: Replace one question with a sequence or contrast question that assesses a distinct detail.

limitations: This is an independent AI pedagogical review for development evidence, not human review or release approval.
The review covers the supplied immutable exercise set and automated audit; it does not report an Internet-wide originality search.
